# refactor(cli): introduce the composition owner and executable

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the error-ownership issue, and builds on it. The next slices (moving the GitHub code,
then the application API) build on this one and also edit `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`.

## What

The `jig` command starts from one clearly named place that does nothing except assemble the
program and start it. Commands, help and installed usage behave exactly as before.

## Why

Startup and wiring currently live inside the GitHub feature folder, which makes that folder an
extra layer above the command line. A dedicated starting point keeps wiring separate from command
handling and application behavior.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Composition", "Dependency lint", and the `composition` row of "Target responsibilities".

- `src/integrations/github/cli.ts` composes the full CLI and starts the executable. Move executable
  startup and command composition to `src/composition/main.ts`, keeping the realpath check that
  makes installed symlinks work. Importing builders or the module must not start a command.
- `package.json`: `bin.jig`, `main` (`./dist/integrations/github/cli.js`) and `scripts.dev`
  (`tsx src/integrations/github/cli.ts`) point at the new executable. Update path-sensitive tests,
  `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts`, and `docs/installation.md` line 52.
- Composition may import `app`, `cli`, `adapters`, `config`, `observers`, `ports` and `domain`.
  It only chooses implementations, constructs them and starts the executable. In this slice it
  still calls the existing app container. Leave the container itself alone; a separate spike
  decides how it changes.
- Dependency Cruiser: add `composition` to `productionModules` in `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`.
  Add the rules "only composition imports `src/cli/` from another owner" and "no other owner
  imports `src/composition/`". The rules cover type-only imports, re-exports and literal dynamic
  imports. `scripts/validate.ts` may keep using CLI parsing helpers; do not let the source-only
  rule break it. Extend `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` with fixtures that accept composition
  importing CLI and reject an adapter, app or nested file importing CLI or composition. Each
  rejection must fail under the named rule, not because of an incidental cycle.
- `src/integrations/github/command.ts` remains a CLI-side command file; the next slice moves it.
  If a temporary edge from `cli` to `integrations` is needed, record it in the PR and do not add a
  forwarding module.

## Done when

- [ ] `node dist/composition/main.js --help` and `node dist/composition/main.js github implement --help`
      work after `npm run build`, and a symlinked executable starts.
- [ ] A spec imports the composition builders without starting a command.
- [ ] Fixtures prove the new rules, including type-only, re-export, dynamic, nested and
      disconnected offenders.
- [ ] Executable paths in `package.json`, the tests and the docs point at `src/composition/main.ts`.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/57

docs.design:
# Goal

Introduce `src/composition/main.ts` as the single executable entry and full-program composition owner. Preserve commands, help, version output, installed symlink execution, import safety and shutdown behavior.

# Context

- `src/integrations/github/cli.ts` currently exports `buildJigCli()`, combines `src/cli/main.ts`'s `buildCli()` with `registerGithubCommands()`, and starts parsing only when the realpath of the invoked executable matches the module path. It awaits `exitWhenDone()` after parsing.
- `src/cli/main.ts` owns core command registration and package-version presentation. `src/integrations/github/command.ts` owns GitHub command translation but remains physically inside integrations. It imports CLI helpers and existing GitHub implementations.
- `src/app/container.ts` owns existing construction and application lifecycle wiring. This slice preserves that implementation and its callers.
- `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` owns `productionModules`, erased-edge analysis, folder-level cycle enforcement and source dependency rules. `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs` recursively discovers production files, checks ownership and runs a separate runtime-cycle analysis. Its temporary-repository regression tests live in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`.
- GitHub isolation currently appears in Dependency Cruiser, overlapping ESLint entries and the custom scanner in `src/boundary.spec.ts`. Moving composition outside integrations makes those restrictions obsolete.
- Package executable metadata, development scripts, E2E invocation paths and public architecture/install references name the existing entry.
- House rules require composition to wire rather than own policy, expected failures to remain Results, and boundary enforcement to stay in the existing dependency pipeline.

# Chosen approach

Move `buildJigCli()` and guarded startup together to `src/composition/main.ts`, with its colocated spec. Preserve the shebang, optional dependency parameters, realpath comparison, `parseAsync(process.argv)` call and subsequent `exitWhenDone()` call. Remove the old executable module without a forwarding export. Building or importing commands must not parse arguments or initiate application work.

Composition owns assembling the complete command tree and starting the executable. CLI retains declarations, parsing and terminal presentation. Application construction and lifecycle remain in their current app implementation; this slice does not introduce a second container or relocate policy.

Register composition in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, where `productionModules` actually lives, rather than duplicating the list in the runner. Permit its specified dependencies on app, cli, adapters, config, observers, ports, domain and failures. The specification includes failures even though the request's dependency list omits it; follow the specification and record this discrepancy in the PR.

Add named production-source rules, proposed as `only-composition-imports-cli` and `composition-is-not-imported-by-other-owners`. Allow same-owner imports and exclude spec importers. Match resolved paths so type-only imports, re-exports, literal dynamic imports and normalized nested paths receive the same treatment. Scope restrictions to `src/` so repository tooling such as `scripts/validate.ts` can continue importing CLI parsing helpers.

Represent the transitional GitHub command explicitly: `src/integrations/github/command.ts` is semantically CLI-owned but remains at its required path. Give exactly that production file permission to import CLI helpers; do not exempt the integrations directory. Composition temporarily imports that command and the existing `GithubPort` type. Restrict composition's temporary integrations access to those concrete files. Document these transitional dependencies and their removal in the following GitHub relocation slice.

Keep Dependency Cruiser's existing physical-folder cycle accounting during this transition. With the command still physically grouped under integrations, its CLI-helper edges remain integrations-to-cli, while composition points to both owners. Do not also add a physical cli-to-integrations registration edge, which would produce an artificial folder cycle. The command's existing outgoing integrations dependencies remain unchanged. This deliberately distinguishes temporary filesystem placement from semantic command ownership without introducing a second dependency analyzer or disabling cycle checks.

Remove `github-is-isolated`, the corresponding fixture expectations, the obsolete ESLint GitHub import restrictions and `src/boundary.spec.ts`. Preserve unrelated ESLint package restrictions, including the current app-only Awilix restriction while container work remains deferred.

The specification describes the eventual removal of integrations and container-free application access. This slice implements only the requested composition boundary: integrations remains registered until its contents move, and application API/container restrictions remain deferred. Record these staged deviations, the exact command exception and the failures allowance in the PR.

Update package `bin.jig` and `main` to the built `dist/composition/main.js` entry and `scripts.dev` to `tsx src/composition/main.ts`. Update executable tests and current public references in place, including architecture diagrams and ownership descriptions.

# Alternatives considered

1. **Move GitHub command handling and the application container now.** This would permit the final folder-based policy immediately, but expands into subsequent slices and makes this change depend on the unresolved construction-mechanism spike. Rejected to preserve the specified scope and lifecycle behavior.
2. **Keep startup under integrations, or retain a forwarding executable there.** This reduces path churn but leaves multiple entry locations and preserves the feature folder's composition responsibility. Rejected because the requested ownership change requires a single new executable with no forwarding module.
3. **Exempt all integrations from the CLI rule or disable folder-cycle checks.** This is simpler than documenting the transition but permits unrelated future violations. Rejected in favor of an exact-file command exception, restricted composition imports and unchanged cycle enforcement.

# Assumptions

- The error-ownership work is present; existing failure definitions and behavior remain unchanged.
- The GitHub relocation slice follows this one and removes the temporary command exception and composition-to-integrations dependencies when their subjects move.
- Node 26.13.0 is the required validation runtime.
- Current constructor/container usage is an intentional intermediate state, not a pattern newly endorsed by this slice.
- Built help and import-safety subprocesses exercise no agent commands and require no publication credentials.

# Non-goals

No application API redesign, container decision, lifecycle rewrite, GitHub implementation redistribution, new settings, dependency framework or source scanner. No changes to commands, flags, defaults, configuration precedence, failure tags/messages, exit codes, recovery, credentials or sandbox behavior. No host agent execution, GitHub publication, version bump or release tag.

# Affected areas

- Move `src/integrations/github/cli.ts` and its spec to `src/composition/main.ts` and `main.spec.ts`.
- Update `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, dependency fixtures and, only where needed, the existing dependency runner integration.
- Reconcile `eslint.config.*` and remove `src/boundary.spec.ts`.
- Update `package.json`, matching package metadata if applicable, `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts` and other path-sensitive tests.
- Update `docs/installation.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and other current guides naming the moved entry. Preserve historical records as history.
- Leave `src/app/container.ts`, application lifecycle and `src/integrations/github/command.ts` behavior unchanged.
docs.plan:
## Step 1 — Move executable composition and preserve startup behavior

Move the executable and its colocated spec to `src/composition/main.ts` and `main.spec.ts`. Adjust relative imports while preserving `buildJigCli()`'s signature, core/GitHub command registration, shebang, realpath guard, parse ordering and shutdown call. Remove the old executable without forwarding exports.

Update package bin/main/dev references and all path-sensitive test invocations, including `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts`. Preserve existing command-composition and version tests. Add a subprocess import-safety test that imports the new module, constructs its builder and reaches an explicit completion marker without command output or process termination. Use a benign argument such as `--version` to expose accidental parsing safely.

## Step 2 — Enforce the composition boundary with the explicit transition

Add composition to the canonical production-owner list and failures importer policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`. Add its source dependency allowlist, including only the two temporary GitHub paths needed by the moved builder.

Implement named source-only CLI and composition import restrictions. Permit same-owner access, spec imports and tooling outside `src/`. Allow only the exact retained `integrations/github/command.ts` file to import CLI helpers as the transitional CLI-owned command. Keep existing physical-folder cycle analysis and runtime file-cycle checks; introduce no cli-to-integrations registration edge or new scanner.

Remove obsolete GitHub isolation from Dependency Cruiser and overlapping ESLint configurations, and delete `src/boundary.spec.ts`. Retain unrelated package and architectural restrictions, including app-only Awilix usage. Keep integrations registered until the next slice moves its remaining production files.

## Step 3 — Prove dependency enforcement and executable behavior

Extend the existing temporary-repository fixtures to accept composition-to-CLI imports, same-owner imports, the exact transitional command imports and permitted composition dependencies. Include a positive tooling case for CLI parsing-helper access and preserve spec access.

Reject adapter, app, CLI and other production-owner imports of composition as applicable; reject non-composition cross-owner CLI imports except the exact retained command. Cover ordinary imports, erased type imports, re-exports, literal dynamic imports, normalized nested paths and disconnected files. Include a neighboring integrations file to prove the command exception is narrow, and an unrelated integrations target to prove composition's temporary allowance is narrow.

Each negative fixture must have resolvable targets and no incidental cycle. Assert failure under the intended named rule and the offending paths. Retain existing tests for erased-edge owner cycles, runtime cycles, production-to-spec imports, unowned sources and resolution/package checks.

After building, verify root help, `github implement --help`, version output and execution through a temporary symlink to the built executable. Verify built-module import safety in a subprocess. Use only help/version/import invocations; do not invoke live E2E agent or publication actions.

## Step 4 — Update current ownership and executable documentation

Update installation commands, CONTRIBUTING's code map, workflow ownership descriptions and the architecture HTML, including interactive labels and obsolete GitHub isolation claims. Search current guides and tests for both source and built forms of the old entry and correct applicable references.

Describe composition as the executable/full-program wiring owner, CLI as the command translation owner and app as retaining existing construction/lifecycle implementation for this slice. State the exact transitional GitHub command placement and dependencies without presenting the eventual architecture as already implemented. Add no new guide or changelog solely for the move.

## Step 5 — Run required verification and prepare review evidence

Use pinned Node 26.13.0 from the repository root. Run `npm run lint:dependencies`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation`. Run the built executable smoke checks after build. Fix failures and repeat affected checks; report any environment limitation accurately rather than claiming a pass.

Prepare PR evidence describing each moved concept's owner and rationale, import-safety and symlink results, named-rule fixture coverage and validation outcomes. Record that the production owner list resides in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, that failures is allowed by the specification, and that the exact command exception and composition-to-integrations edges are temporary. Explain why application/container and remaining integrations work are deferred. Do not publish, create release tags or change the package version.
